page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-2 is an entry-level compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture within the N1 server family. It features 2 virtual CPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon processor core running at 2.3 GHz with Hyper-Threading enabled. The system includes 2.0 GB of total system memory, equating to 0.9 GB per vCPU, alongside 45 MB of L3 CPU cache. Hardware features include AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction extensions. The instance utilizes dedicated CPU allocation, but contains no local NVMe storage, no GPUs, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a stress-ng multi-core performance score of 1408.88 and a single-core score of 1086.39. PassMark CPU execution measures at 1638.85. Memory subsystem tests show uncached large-block read bandwidth of 13.22 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 11.3 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, the instance achieves 1.35 million Redis SET operations per second and static web serving throughput of 1.51 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning workloads, prompt processing on a 135M model yields 65.68 tokens per second and text generation reaches 38.74 tokens per second.

The core tradeoff of the n1-highcpu-2 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio and modest overall bandwidth, which limits suitability for memory-heavy or highly concurrent applications. However, dedicated CPU allocation delivers predictable compute performance without credit-based throttling. This instance is best fitted for light background microservices, basic static web serving, minor utility scripts, and low-footprint batch jobs.
